tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

{"file_path": "bingge-bbq/work/build_logo.py", "content": "# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Build the Bingge BBQ identity as SVG, then rasterize with resvg."""
import math
import os

OUT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(OUT)

# ---------------- palette ----------------
C = {
    "bg0": "#1D2512",
    "bg1": "#37421F",
    "bg2": "#2A3419",
    "camo1": "#3E4A24",
    "camo2": "#222B14",
    "olive": "#4C5929",
    "olive_lt": "#68763C",
    "olive_dk": "#2E381A",
    "cream": "#F3E7CD",
    "cream_dk": "#E3D2B0",
    "sand": "#D8C39D",
    "orange": "#E86A24",
    "amber": "#F2A63B",
    "ember": "#F6C45A",
    "brass": "#B08D4F",
    "char": "#191E10",
    "meat": "#A5522A",
    "meat_dk": "#743219",
    "meat_lt": "#C9743C",
    "wood": "#D8B37A",
    "wood_dk": "#AE854D",
    "log": "#4A3320",
    "log_lt": "#6B4A2B",
}

FONT = "Noto Sans SC"


def f(v):
    return f"{v:.2f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")


def defs():
    return f'''<defs>
  <radialGradient id="bg" cx="50%" cy="40%" r="78%">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="{C['bg1']}"/>
    <stop offset="0.62" stop-color="{C['bg2']}"/>
    <stop offset="1" stop-color="{C['bg0']}"/>
  </radialGradient>
  <linearGradient id="flame" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="{C['amber']}"/>
    <stop offset="0.55" stop-color="{C['orange']}"/>
    <stop offset="1" stop-color="#C94F1B"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <linearGradient id="patch" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0.75" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="#F8EFD9"/>
    <stop offset="0.58" stop-color="{C['cream']}"/>
    <stop offset="1" stop-color="{C['cream_dk']}"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <linearGradient id="helmet" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0.8" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="#61703A"/>
    <stop offset="0.52" stop-color="{C['olive']}"/>
    <stop offset="1" stop-color="#39451F"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <linearGradient id="brim" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="#48552A"/>
    <stop offset="1" stop-color="#283115"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <clipPath id="patchClip"><circle cx="300" cy="300" r="270"/></clipPath>
</defs>'''


def topo_paths(seed=0, n=7, stroke=C["sand"], opacity=0.28):
    """Hand-authored wavy contour paths for the patch / background."""
    paths = [
        "M 36 418 C 92 366 150 394 204 362 C 256 330 320 332 372 356 C 424 380 474 372 526 338 C 560 316 588 318 610 332",
        "M 30 452 C 92 398 152 428 208 394 C 260 362 320 364 374 388 C 428 412 480 402 532 368 C 566 346 596 348 620 362",
        "M 30 486 C 94 432 154 460 212 426 C 264 396 322 398 376 420 C 430 442 484 432 536 398 C 570 376 598 380 622 392",
        "M 42 312 C 100 276 148 294 200 268 C 254 242 306 246 356 268 C 410 292 462 286 512 254 C 550 230 584 232 614 248",
        "M 58 246 C 112 214 160 228 208 206 C 258 184 306 188 354 208 C 406 230 456 224 504 196 C 542 174 584 176 616 192",
    ]
    out = []
    for i, d in enumerate(paths[:n]):
        out.append(
            f'<path d="{d}" fill="none" stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{1.4 + (i % 3) * 0.4:.1f}" opacity="{opacity - 0.02 * (i % 4):.3f}"/>'
        )
    return "".join(out)


def pine(x, base_y, h, w, color, opacity=0.42):
    """Simple layered pine silhouette."""
    tiers = 3
    parts = []
    trunk_w = max(3, w * 0.11)
    parts.append(
        f'<rect x="{f(x-trunk_w/2)}" y="{f(base_y-h*0.16)}" width="{f(trunk_w)}" height="{f(h*0.18)}" rx="{f(trunk_w/2)}" fill="{color}" opacity="{opacity}"/>'
    )
    for i in range(tiers):
        ty = base_y - h * (0.14 + i * 0.25)
        tw = w * (1 - i * 0.22)
        th = h * (0.40 - i * 0.05)
        parts.append(
            f'<path d="M {f(x)} {f(ty-th)} L {f(x+tw/2)} {f(ty)} L {f(x-tw/2)} {f(ty)} Z" fill="{color}" opacity="{opacity}"/>'
        )
    return "".join(parts)


def meat_cube(x, y, angle, side=30, z=0):
    """A threaded, charred meat cube."""
    h = side * 1.06
    return f'''<g transform="translate({f(x)} {f(y)}) rotate({f(angle)})">
  <rect x="{f(-side/2)}" y="{f(-h/2)}" width="{f(side)}" height="{f(h)}" rx="5" fill="{C['meat_dk']}"/>
  <rect x="{f(-side/2+2)}" y="{f(-h/2+2)}" width="{f(side-4)}" height="{f(h-5)}" rx="4" fill="{C['meat']}"/>
  <path d="M {f(-side/2+4)} {f(-h/2+8)} Q 0 {f(-h/2+3)} {f(side/2-4)} {f(-h/2+9)}" fill="none" stroke="{C['meat_lt']}" stroke-width="3.2" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.9"/>
  <path d="M {f(-side/2+5)} {f(h/2-8)} Q 0 {f(h/2-3)} {f(side/2-5)} {f(h/2-9)}" fill="none" stroke="#5A2814" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.75"/>
</g>'''


def skewer(p0, p1, meat_ts=(0.17, 0.31, 0.45), angle=None):
    """A bamboo skewer with a pointed tip at p1 and three meat cubes."""
    x0, y0 = p0
    x1, y1 = p1
    dx, dy = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
    length = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    ux, uy = dx / length, dy / length
    a = math.degrees(math.atan2(dy, dx))
    if angle is not None:
        a = angle
    parts = []
    # bamboo stick
    parts.append(
        f'<line x1="{f(x0)}" y1="{f(y0)}" x2="{f(x1)}" y2="{f(y1)}" stroke="{C["wood_dk"]}" stroke-width="8" stroke-linecap="round"/>'
    )
    parts.append(
        f'<line x1="{f(x0)}" y1="{f(y0)}" x2="{f(x1)}" y2="{f(y1)}" stroke="{C["wood"]}" stroke-width="4.6" stroke-linecap="round"/>'
    )
    # pointed tip
    tip_x = x1 + ux * 8
    tip_y = y1 + uy * 8
    nx, ny = -uy, ux
    parts.append(
        f'<path d="M {f(x1+nx*4.6)} {f(y1+ny*4.6)} L {f(tip_x)} {f(tip_y)} L {f(x1-nx*4.6)} {f(y1-ny*4.6)} Z" fill="{C["wood"]}"/>'
    )
    # meat cubes sit on the lower half
    for t in meat_ts:
        cx, cy = x0 + dx * t, y0 + dy * t
        parts.append(meat_cube(cx, cy, a))
    return "".join(parts)


def helmet(show_char=True):
    """Field helmet, drawn to read at small size."""
    p = []
    # chin strap loops (behind brim)
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 198 338 C 202 386 226 414 258 430" fill="none" stroke="{C["olive_dk"]}" stroke-width="9" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.9"/>'
    )
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 402 338 C 398 386 374 414 342 430" fill="none" stroke="{C["olive_dk"]}" stroke-width="9" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.9"/>'
    )
    # dome
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 180 326 C 180 230 228 166 300 166 C 372 166 420 230 420 326 Z" fill="url(#helmet)"/>'
    )
    # dome shadow
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 180 300 C 218 330 382 330 420 300 L 420 326 C 382 344 218 344 180 326 Z" fill="{C["olive_dk"]}" opacity="0.72"/>'
    )
    # left highlight
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 211 310 C 209 242 242 192 286 178 C 255 210 238 260 238 312 Z" fill="{C["olive_lt"]}" opacity="0.55"/>'
    )
    # crown ridges
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 297 166 C 290 216 290 270 297 326" fill="none" stroke="{C["olive_lt"]}" stroke-width="4" opacity="0.55"/>'
    )
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 306 167 C 313 216 313 270 306 326" fill="none" stroke="{C["olive_dk"]}" stroke-width="3" opacity="0.45"/>'
    )
    # brim
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 150 326 C 210 311 390 311 450 326 C 459 329 459 339 450 342 C 390 360 210 360 150 342 C 141 339 141 329 150 326 Z" fill="url(#brim)"/>'
    )
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 158 330 C 218 317 382 317 442 330" fill="none" stroke="{C["olive_lt"]}" stroke-width="3" opacity="0.65"/>'
    )
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 168 344 C 230 359 370 359 432 344" fill="none" stroke="#1D2510" stroke-width="4" opacity="0.55"/>'
    )
    # side rivets
    for x in (176, 424):
        p.append(f'<circle cx="{x}" cy="335" r="4.2" fill="{C["cream"]}" opacity="0.55"/>')
    if show_char:
        p.append(
            f'<text x="300" y="307" text-anchor="middle" font-family="{FONT}" font-weight="900" font-size="78" fill="{C["cream"]}">兵</text>'
        )
        p.append(f'<rect x="280" y="314" width="40" height="4" rx="2" fill="{C["amber"]}" opacity="0.9"/>')
    return "".join(p)


def emblem(show_arc=True, show_char=True):
    """600 x 600 local badge."""
    p = []
    # rings
    p.append(f'<circle cx="300" cy="300" r="288" fill="{C["char"]}"/>')
    p.append(f'<circle cx="300" cy="300" r="280" fill="{C["olive"]}"/>')

    # tent

    )
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 300 398 L 334 470 L 266 470 Z" fill="{C["olive_dk"]}" opacity="0.55"/>'
    )
    p.append(
        f'<path d="M 300 372 L 300 470" fill="none" stroke="{C["cream"]}" stroke-width="2" opacity="0.40"/>'

        )

def square_logo(size=1024):
    badge_scale = 286 / 288  # emblem outer diameter 576 -> r 286
    tx = size / 2 - 300 * badge_scale
    ty = 386 - 300 * badge_scale
    return f'''<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{size}" height="{size}" viewBox="0 0 1024 1024">
{defs()}
<rect width="1024" height="1024" fill="url(#bg)"/>
<g opacity="0.055">{topo_paths(n=5, stroke=C["cream"], opacity=1)}</g>

<rect x="44" y="44" width="936" height="936" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="{C["cream"]}" stroke-width="1" opacity="0.12"/>

<g transform="translate({f(tx)} {f(ty)}) scale({f(badge_scale)})">{emblem()}</g>
<g>
  <line x1="332" y1="730" x2="474" y2="730" stroke="{C["cream"]}" stroke-width="2" opacity="0.34"/>
  <line x1="550" y1="730" x2="692" y2="730" stroke="{C["cream"]}" stroke-width="2" opacity="0.34"/>
  <rect x="505" y="723" width="14" height="14" rx="2" transform="rotate(45 512 730)" fill="{C["orange"]}"/>
  <text x="512" y="836" text-anchor="middle" font-family="{FONT}" font-weight="900" font-size="154" letter-spacing="6" fill="{C["cream"]}">兵哥烧烤</text>
  <text x="512" y="894" text-anchor="middle" font-family="{FONT}" font-weight="700" font-size="24" letter-spacing="5.2" fill="{C["brass"]}">BINGGE BBQ · FIELD GRILL</text>
</g>
</svg>'''


def icon(size=1024):
    s = 0.805
    tx = size / 2 - 300 * s
    ty = size / 2 - 300 * s
    return f'''<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{size}" height="{size}" viewBox="0 0 1024 1024">
{defs()}
<rect width="1024" height="1024" rx="0" fill="url(#bg)"/>
<g opacity="0.06">{topo_paths(n=4, stroke=C["cream"], opacity=1)}</g>
<rect x="26" y="26" width="972" height="972" rx="12" fill="none" stroke="{C["cream"]}" stroke-width="2" opacity="0.22"/>
<g transform="translate({f(tx)} {f(ty)}) scale({f(s)})">{emblem(show_arc=False)}</g>
</svg>'''


def horizontal(w=1600, h=600):
    # badge diameter 470 at left
    s = 235 / 288
    tx = 104 + (288 - 300) * s
    ty = h / 2 - 300 * s
    return f'''<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{w}" height="{h}" viewBox="0 0 1600 600">
{defs()}
<rect width="1600" height="600" fill="url(#bg)"/>
<g opacity="0.06">{topo_paths(n=4, stroke=C["cream"], opacity=1)}</g>
<rect x="24" y="24" width="1552" height="552" rx="12" fill="none" stroke="{C["cream"]}" stroke-width="2" opacity="0.24"/>
<g transform="translate({f(tx)} {f(ty)}) scale({f(s)})">{emblem()}</g>
<g>

  <text x="648" y="286" font-family="{FONT}" font-weight="900" font-size="150" letter-spacing="5" fill="{C["cream"]}">兵哥烧烤</text>
  <text x="652" y="350" font-family="{FONT}" font-weight="700" font-size="27" letter-spacing="6" fill="{C["brass"]}">BINGGE BBQ · FIELD GRILL</text>
  <text x="652" y="401" font-family="{FONT}" font-weight="500" font-size="25" letter-spacing="3" fill="{C["cream"]}" opacity="0.72">野营炭烤 · 现串现火 · 城市里的那口野味</text>
</g>
</svg>'''


def mono():
    """One-color cream-on-transparent stamp for packaging."""
    s = 0.9
    tx = 512 - 300 * s
    ty = 470 - 300 * s
    # override emblem colors via CSS? build a simplified monochrome badge here
    return f'''<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1024" height="1024" viewBox="0 0 1024 1024">
<g fill="none" stroke="{C["cream"]}" stroke-width="14">
  <circle cx="512" cy="452" r="330"/>
  <circle cx="512" cy="452" r="296" stroke-width="4" stroke-dasharray="12 14"/>
</g>
<g transform="translate({f(tx)} {f(ty)}) scale({f(s)})" opacity="0.98">
  <g fill="{C["cream"]}">
    {helmet().replace(C["cream"], C["cream"])}
  </g>
</g>
<text x="512" y="900" text-anchor="middle" font-family="{FONT}" font-weight="900" font-size="126" letter-spacing="8" fill="{C["cream"]}">兵哥烧烤</text>
</svg>'''


if __name__ == "__main__":
    assets = os.path.join(ROOT, "assets")
    os.makedirs(assets, exist_ok=True)
    files = {
        "logo-square.svg": square_logo(),
        "logo-icon.svg": icon(),
        "logo-horizontal.svg": horizontal(),
        "logo-mono.svg": mono(),
    }
    for name, svg in files.items():
        path = os.path.join(assets, name)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(svg)
        print("wrote", path)
"}

{"file_path": "bingge-bbq/work/build_logo.py", "content": "# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Build the Bingge BBQ identity as SVG, then rasterize with resvg."""
import math
import os

OUT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(OUT)

# ---------------- palette ----------------
C = {
    "bg0": "#1D2512",
    "bg1": "#37421F",
    "bg2": "#2A3419",
    "camo1": "#3E4A24",
    "camo2": "#222B14",
    "olive": "#4C5929",
    "olive_lt": "#68763C",
    "olive_dk": "#2E381A",
    "cream": "#F3E7CD",
    "cream_dk": "#E3D2B0",
    "sand": "#D8C39D",
    "orange": "#E86A24",
    "amber": "#F2A63B",
    "ember": "#F6C45A",
    "brass": "#B08D4F",
    "char": "#191E10",
    "meat": "#A5522A",
    "meat_dk": "#743219",
    "meat_lt": "#C9743C",
    "wood": "#D8B37A",
    "wood_dk": "#AE854D",
    "log": "#4A3320",
    "log_lt": "#6B4A2B",
}

FONT = "Noto Sans SC"


def f(v):
    return f"{v:.2f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")


def defs():
    return f'''<defs>
  <radialGradient id="bg" cx="50%" cy="40%" r="78%">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="{C['bg1']}"/>
    <stop offset="0.62" stop-color="{C['bg2']}"/>
    <stop offset="1" stop-color="{C['bg0']}"/>
  </radialGradient>
  <linearGradient id="flame" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="{C['amber']}"/>
    <stop offset="0.55" stop-color="{C['orange']}"/>
    <stop offset="1" stop-color="#C94F1B"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <linearGradient id="patch" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0.75" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="#F8EFD9"/>
    <stop offset="0.58" stop-color="{C['cream']}"/>
    <stop offset="1" stop-color="{C['cream_dk']}"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <linearGradient id="helmet" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0.8" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="#61703A"/>
    <stop offset="0.52" stop-color="{C['olive']}"/>
    <stop offset="1" stop-color="#39451F"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <linearGradient id="brim" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="#48552A"/>
    <stop offset="1" stop-color="#283115"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <clipPath id="patchClip"><circle cx="300" cy="300" r="270"/></clipPath>
</defs>'''


def topo_paths(seed=0, n=7, stroke=C["sand"], opacity=0.28):
    """Hand-authored wavy contour paths for the patch / background."""
    paths = [
        "M 36 418 C 92 366 150 394 204 362 C 256 330 320 332 372 356 C 424 380 474 372 526 338 C 560 316 588 318 610 332",
        "M 30 452 C 92 398 152 428 208 394 C 260 362 320 364 374 388 C 428 412 480 402 532 368 C 566 346 596 348 620 362",
        "M 30 486 C 94 432 154 460 212 426 C 264 396 322 398 376 420 C 430 442 484 432 536 398 C 570 376 598 380 622 392",
        "M 42 312 C 100 276 148 294 200 268 C 254 242 306 246 356 268 C 410 292 462 286 512 254 C 550 230 584 232 614 248",
        "M 58 246 C 112 214 160 228 208 206 C 258 184 306 188 354 208 C 406 230 456 224 504 196 C 542 174 584 176 616 192",
    ]
    out = []
    for i, d in enumerate(paths[:n]):
        out.append(
            f'<path d="{d}" fill="none" stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{1.4 + (i % 3) * 0.4:.1f}" opacity="{opacity - 0.02 * (i % 4):.3f}"/>'
        )
    return "".join(out)


def pine(x, base_y, h, w, color, opacity=0.42):
    """Simple layered pine silhouette."""
    tiers = 3
    parts = []
    trunk_w = max(3, w * 0.11)
    parts.append(
        f'<rect x="{f(x-trunk_w/2)}" y="{f(base_y-h*0.16)}" width="{f(trunk_w)}" height="{f(h*0.18)}" rx="{f(trunk_w/2)}" fill="{color}" opacity="{opacity}"/>'
    )
    for i in range(tiers):
        ty = base_y - h * (0.14 + i * 0.25)
        tw = w * (1 - i * 0.22)
        th = h * (0.40 - i * 0.05)
        parts.append(
            f'<path d="M {f(x)} {f(ty-th)} L {f(x+tw/2)} {f(ty)} L {f(x-tw/2)} {f(ty)} Z" fill="{color}" opacity="{opacity}"/>'
        )
    return "".join(parts)


def meat_cube(x, y, angle, side=30, z=0):
    """A threaded, charred meat cube."""
    h = side * 1.06
    return f'''<g transform="translate({f(x)} {f(y)}) rotate({f(angle)})">
  <rect x="{f(-side/2)}" y="{f(-h/2)}" width="{f(side)}" height="{f(h)}" rx="5" fill="{C['meat_dk']}"/>
  <rect x="{f(-side/2+2)}" y="{f(-h/2+2)}" width="{f(side-4)}" height="{f(h-5)}" rx="4" fill="{C['meat']}"/>
  <path d="M {f(-side/2+4)} {f(-h/2+8)} Q 0 {f(-h/2+3)} {f(side/2-4)} {f(-h/2+9)}" fill="none" stroke="{C['meat_lt']}" stroke-width="3.2" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.9"/>
  <path d="M {f(-side/2+5)} {f(h/2-8)} Q 0 {f(h/2-3)} {f(side/2-5)} {f(h/2-9)}" fill="none" stroke="#5A2814" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.75"/>
</g>'''


def skewer(p0, p1, meat_ts=(0.17, 0.31, 0.45), angle=None):
    """A bamboo skewer with a pointed tip at p1 and three meat cubes."""
    x0, y0 = p0
    x1, y1 = p1
    dx, dy = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
    length = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    ux, uy = dx / length, dy / length
    a = math.degrees(math.atan2(dy, dx))
    if angle is not None:
        a = angle
    parts = []

First draft. Issues:
1. Wordmark overlaps divider lines and orange diamond. Divider at y=730, Chinese font baseline 836 with font size 154 → glyph top about 690, so it overlaps divider. Need divider higher or wordmark lower/smaller. Move divider to 700? Badge bottom 672, little gap. Better remove divider or move it into gap at y=700, and wordmark down to 860. Or remove divider entirely and use a small emblem between badge and wordmark. The line crossing text looks bad. We'll adjust.
2. The logo text is large, bottom English close to border? English baseline 894, bottom 950; border 950. The English text bottom ~900, okay, but the border almost touches. Could move up.
3. The badge icon: helmet appears more like a hard hat / bowler than military helmet. Brim is too straight/flat and dome too round; need more military M1 helmet shape: wider brim with downward curve, dome a bit flatter and flared at bottom, chin straps visible. Currently the chin straps are hidden (drawn behind dome, then flame covers), only tiny loops near sides. The "兵" text on helmet is good but might look like a construction helmet. Need stronger helmet silhouette: a slight dome with a raised front, brim curving down at sides, and a chin strap. Maybe a WWI Brodie helmet (flat wide brim) would read military but also construction. M1 helmet with a curved brim and side flare is best.
4. The flame is mostly hidden behind the helmet and meat; only yellow "M" shape. It looks like a cartoon face? The flame tongues are barely visible. Need move icon composition: raise helmet, lower flame, reduce meat cubes, maybe show flames better.
5. Skewers: meat cubes look like a chain/pretzel across the fire. Too many and too big, blocking flame. Need refine: one skewer each side with 2-3 smaller cubes, placed diagonally outward, not crossing in front of flame center. Or put skewers resting on top of a grill grate, with the flame below.
6. Curved text is overlapped by meat/skewers and pines, hard to read, too low. The text is inside the fire area. Need move it lower or remove. At the bottom, it overlaps the pines/ground. Remove curved text or place at y 520 with a clear band. There's space at bottom of patch (y 500-570). Move arc radius to 245, bottom y=545.
7. Topo lines inside patch are very faint but okay; background topo lines only on left due to coordinates. Need scale background pattern.
8. Badge seems small relative to the wordmark? 576 diameter vs wordmark 620; okay but visually the badge is dense. Could enlarge badge to 620 and reduce wordmark to 140. Delivery platform wants icon large. But text should be legible. Balance: badge diameter ~600, wordmark 140. 
9. Outer border: nice but corners maybe too decorative. Fine.
10. English letterspacing too wide? It looks good but "BINGGE BBQ · FIELD GRILL" near bottom. Fine.
11. Color: military green reads. Fire is orange. Cream nice. The icon overall feels like a cartoon construction hard-hat BBQ; need more rugged/military, less cute. The 兵 character on the helmet is a good brand element but could be more integrated. Maybe remove underline (looks like a smile? the amber line under 兵 reads as a mouth, making the helmet a face). Indeed the helmet looks like a face: 兵 as eyes? It looks like a hard hat with a face. The amber line under 兵 makes it whimsical. Remove it. The 兵 should sit on a badge plate, not a mouth.
12. The flame is behind the "face" so it looks like a beard/mustache. Need change composition.

Let's rethink icon composition to be more readable and premium.

Option: **Helmet on a grill grate**, flame below, crossed skewers above/behind. Currently flame under helmet is like a face. Maybe that's okay if helmet is clearly a helmet and flame is separate. But the brim cutting across the flame makes it look like a face. We can make the helmet larger and higher, and the flame lower with a clear gap; the brim won't intersect flame. Maybe add a grill grate line between helmet and flame? A grill grate at y 365, with flames below. Then the helmet floats above the grill; not physically connected. Could be a badge composition: helmet as crest above a grill.

Alternative: **Helmet as grill lid** with flames coming out from under the brim is conceptually nice, but visually can look like a face. Add a clear grill grate below the brim and have flames below/around; the helmet is the lid. Add a handle on top of the helmet (like a grill lid handle), making it a "helmet grill". A small D-handle on top would make it read as a grill lid, but also look like a helmet with a handle (cute). Hmm.

Maybe remove the 兵 from the helmet and put a **flame badge** or **star** instead; then it won't look like a face. The helmet can sit above crossed skewers and flame with a clear gap. The wordmark tells the name.

Let's look at icon-only to judge.

def wobbly_ring(cx, cy, rx, ry, wobble=0.05, n=16, phase=0.0, samples=1.0):
    pts = []
    for i in range(n):
        a = 2 * math.pi * i / n
        r = 1 + wobble * math.sin(3 * a + phase) + 0.45 * wobble * math.sin(5 * a + phase * 1.7)
        pts.append((cx + rx * r * math.cos(a), cy + ry * r * math.sin(a)))
    d = f"M {f(pts[0][0])} {f(pts[0][1])}"
    for i in range(n):
        p0 = pts[(i - 1) % n]
        p1 = pts[i]
        p2 = pts[(i + 1) % n]
        p3 = pts[(i + 2) % n]
        c1 = (p1[0] + (p2[0] - p0[0]) / 6, p1[1] + (p2[1] - p0[1]) / 6)
        c2 = (p2[0] - (p3[0] - p1[0]) / 6, p2[1] - (p3[1] - p1[1]) / 6)
        d += f" C {f(c1[0])} {f(c1[1])} {f(c2[0])} {f(c2[1])} {f(p2[0])} {f(p2[1])}"
    return d + " Z"

def skewer(p0, p1, meat_ts=(0.18, 0.36), side=30):

    ang = math.degrees(math.atan2(dy, dx))
    p = []
    p.append(f'<line x1="{f(x0)}" y1="{f(y0)}" x2="{f(x1)}" y2="{f(y1)}" stroke="{C["wood_dk"]}" stroke-width="8" stroke-linecap="round"/>')

    nx, ny = -uy, ux
    p.append(f'<path d="M {f(x1+nx*4.2)} {f(y1+ny*4.2)} L {f(tip_x)} {f(tip_y)} L {f(x1-nx*4.2)} {f(y1-ny*4.2)} Z" fill="{C["wood"]}"/>')

def wobbly_ring(cx, cy, rx, ry, wobble=0.05, n=16, phase=0.0, samples=1.0):
    pts = []
    for i in range(n):
        a = 2 * math.pi * i / n
        r = 1 + wobble * math.sin(3 * a + phase) + 0.45 * wobble * math.sin(5 * a + phase * 1.7)
        pts.append((cx + rx * r * math.cos(a), cy + ry * r * math.sin(a)))
    d = f"M {f(pts[0][0])} {f(pts[0][1])}"
    for i in range(n):
        p0 = pts[(i - 1) % n]
        p1 = pts[i]
        p2 = pts[(i + 1) % n]
        p3 = pts[(i + 2) % n]
        c1 = (p1[0] + (p2[0] - p0[0]) / 6, p1[1] + (p2[1] - p0[1]) / 6)
        c2 = (p2[0] - (p3[0] - p1[0]) / 6, p2[1] - (p3[1] - p1[1]) / 6)
        d += f" C {f(c1[0])} {f(c1[1])} {f(c2[0])} {f(c2[1])} {f(p2[0])} {f(p2[1])}"
    return d + " Z"

def skewer(p0, p1, meat_ts=(0.18, 0.36), side=30):
    x0, y0 = p0

    length = math.hypot(dx, dy)

    p = []

    nx, ny = -uy, ux
    p.append(f'<path d="M {f(x1+nx*4.2)} {f(y1+ny*4.2)} L {f(tip_x)} {f(tip_y)} L {f(x1-nx*4.2)} {f(y1-ny*4.2)} Z" fill="{C["wood"]}"/>')

def wobbly_ring(cx, cy, rx, ry, wobble=0.05, n=16, phase=0.0, samples=1.0):
    pts = []
    for i in range(n):
        a = 2 * math.pi * i / n
        r = 1 + wobble * math.sin(3 * a + phase) + 0.45 * wobble * math.sin(5 * a + phase * 1.7)
        pts.append((cx + rx * r * math.cos(a), cy + ry * r * math.sin(a)))
    d = f"M {f(pts[0][0])} {f(pts[0][1])}"
    for i in range(n):
        p0 = pts[(i - 1) % n]
        p1 = pts[i]
        p2 = pts[(i + 1) % n]
        p3 = pts[(i + 2) % n]
        c1 = (p1[0] + (p2[0] - p0[0]) / 6, p1[1] + (p2[1] - p0[1]) / 6)
        c2 = (p2[0] - (p3[0] - p1[0]) / 6, p2[1] - (p3[1] - p1[1]) / 6)
        d += f" C {f(c1[0])} {f(c1[1])} {f(c2[0])} {f(c2[1])} {f(p2[0])} {f(p2[1])}"

def wobbly_ring(cx, cy, rx, ry, wobble=0.05, n=16, phase=0.0, samples=1.0):
    pts = []
    for i in range(n):
        a = 2 * math.pi * i / n
        r = 1 + wobble * math.sin(3 * a + phase) + 0.45 * wobble * math.sin(5 * a + phase * 1.7)
        pts.append((cx + rx * r * math.cos(a), cy + ry * r * math.sin(a)))
    d = f"M {f(pts[0][0])} {f(pts[0][1])}"
    for i in range(n):
        p0 = pts[(i - 1) % n]
        p1 = pts[i]
        p2 = pts[(i + 1) % n]
        p3 = pts[(i + 2) % n]
        c1 = (p1[0] + (p2[0] - p0[0]) / 6, p1[1] + (p2[1] - p0[1]) / 6)
        c2 = (p2[0] - (p3[0] - p1[0]) / 6, p2[1] - (p3[1] - p1[1]) / 6)
        d += f" C {f(c1[0])} {f(c1[1])} {f(c2[0])} {f(c2[1])} {f(p2[0])} {f(p2[1])}"
    return d + " Z"

def skewer(p0, p1, meat_ts=(0.18, 0.36), side=30):
    x0, y0 = p0
    x1, y1 = p1

    length = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    ux, uy = dx / length, dy / length
    ang = math.degrees(math.atan2(dy, dx))
    p = []
    p.append(f'<line x1="{f(x0)}" y1="{f(y0)}" x2="{f(x1)}" y2="{f(y1)}" stroke="{C["wood_dk"]}" stroke-width="8" stroke-linecap="round"/>')

    tip_x, tip_y = x1 + ux * 8, y1 + uy * 8
    nx, ny = -uy, ux
    p.append(f'<path d="M {f(x1+nx*4.2)} {f(y1+ny*4.2)} L {f(tip_x)} {f(tip_y)} L {f(x1-nx*4.2)} {f(y1-ny*4.2)} Z" fill="{C["wood"]}"/>')
    for t in meat_ts:
        p.append(meat_cube(x0 + dx * t, y0 + dy * t, ang, side))
    # bamboo handle wrap at the outer end
    hx, hy = x0 - ux * 4, y0 - uy * 4
    p.append(f'<line x1="{f(hx)}" y1="{f(hy)}" x2="{f(hx+ux*16)}" y2="{f(hy+uy*16)}" stroke="#8A5F35" stroke-width="7" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.9"/>')

The 兵 makes it look like a military helmet more, but also like a construction helmet with a sticker. The 兵 character is bold and nice. For a brand called 兵哥, I lean toward the 兵 version, but need improve helmet shape and composition.

Maybe the helmet should be viewed at a slight angle, not straight-on? A 3/4 helmet could look more dynamic and less like a hard hat. But harder to draw. A straight-on helmet is iconic.

Could add a **helmet cover** with a stencil "兵" and a **chin strap** with buckle. The current chin strap hangs like a chin strap (good). The brim all around is military. The high dome is perhaps more like a **paratrooper helmet**? Paratrooper helmets have a lower dome and a cut-down brim. Maybe flatten the dome:
- Current dome top 146, brim 318: height 172, width 260. Ratio 0.66. M1 helmet dome height ~0.55 of width. Flatten to top 165, brim 318: height 153. More military.
- Widen the brim to 300 and make it flatter/horizontal, with a slight downward curve at the front. 
- Add a **front lip** / raised rim at the front, a signature of M1 helmets. Our brim already has a rim line.
- Add **side chinstrap bales** (small metal loops) at the brim sides; we have rivets.
- Add a **helmet band** around the dome with a small buckle at the side. Already there but subtle.
- Make the dome less perfectly symmetrical: slight asymmetry/wear. A few scratches? Adds character.
- Use a darker olive and less glossy gradient; current dome has a strong highlight that makes it look like plastic. Reduce highlight and gradient contrast; use matte olive with a camo cover. This will look more military and less like a toy hard hat. 
- Add a **camo pattern** more visible: 3-4 blobs in dark/light olive at 35%. Camo covers are iconic military. But too much pattern at small size could be noise. Keep 2-3 large blobs, not small.
- Change the shape to a **fritz helmet** (German) silhouette? That has a distinctive flared rim and is strongly military, but may evoke WWII German imagery—avoid. M1 is safer but generic. A modern **combat helmet** with a square-ish cut and side rails could read tactical, but is visually different. A **boonie hat** would read military+camping but no dome. "兵哥" could wear a boonie hat, but a helmet is stronger.
- A **steel pot** / M1 with a camo cover and "兵" is good.

Could add a **small tent silhouette on top of the helmet**? No.

The icon at 1024: mark fills only about 56% of the square? Wait icon v2 uses s=438/288=1.52, r=288*1.52=438, diameter 876, margin 74. Great. Let's view.

At icon size, it's clear but definitely reads as a **hard hat** (construction). The brim all around + high dome. The chin strap helps but still. The fire/skewers look like a little body. The 兵 version would read more military. Need improve.

Also, the skewers look like **two legs with brown shoes**; the V is too vertical and the meat cubes at the ends look like feet. This is a problem. Need change skewer angle/composition to avoid the body metaphor:
- Make skewers **horizontal-ish**, resting across the fire, not V. E.g., one skewer from left to right across the flame at a shallow angle, another crossing it; meat cubes along them. That would clearly be skewers, not legs.
- Or place skewers **behind the helmet**, crossing like an X at the top. But then the fire is separate.
- Or have **one skewer** diagonally across the fire, with 3 meat cubes, and a second skewer at a different angle. Horizontal/diagonal reads food, V reads legs.
- Maybe the fire should be inside a **grill** with a horizontal grate, and skewers laid horizontally on top. This avoids the body. The helmet sits above like a crest. That's a cleaner still life.

Let's redesign lower half:
- A **campfire** at center, logs at bottom.
- A **grill grate** across the fire: 2 horizontal bars at y 400 and 450, with 5 vertical connectors? Or a simple grid in perspective.
- **Two skewers** laid horizontally/diagonally on the grate, with meat cubes, extending beyond the grate left/right. This is clearly BBQ.
- Pines/tent behind.
- Helmet above with a gap, as the "兵" crest.

But a grill grate over a campfire might obscure the flame. We can draw the grate thin dark lines over the flame, with skewers on top. The flame remains visible between bars. 
- Grate: perspective ellipse? For a front view, draw 2 horizontal bars (y 405, 450) and 5 short vertical bars connecting, plus two legs? A rectangular grid in front of the fire looks like a fence. Maybe a **single grill bar** with 4 hanging hooks? Hmm.
- Could draw a **grill grate in perspective**: top edge at y=405 width 260, bottom edge at y=455 width 300, with 6 lines converging. This gives depth and looks like a grill. Skewers lay on top. The fire behind/below. Nice.

Alternative: **one large skewer** held diagonally across the flame, with 3 meat cubes and a handle. This is simple and unmistakable. Add a second skewer crossed behind at a shallower angle with 2 cubes. They form an X but horizontal-ish, not a V. The X could still look like legs but less so if one is near-horizontal.

- Add a **grill bar** under them? Not necessary; they can rest on logs.

The fire shape could be wider and lower, with logs. The skewers horizontal across it. The composition becomes a campfire cookout, not a character.

- Sausage? No.

What about a **grill fork**? No.

Let's test a version with one diagonal skewer and a second behind, horizontal. The icon will be less symmetric, more dynamic and appetizing. The helmet centered above, fire below, skewers across. That should read well.

But the request includes camping; pines/tent remain. Good.

- Add a **small chin strap buckle** at one side, currently there are brass rectangles at strap ends (good).
- Make the brim slightly **asymmetrical** (front dip) and add a raised front rim.
- Add a **helmet cover band** with a stitched edge? Maybe.

# 6. Move patch tag up, clear of stitch ring
s = s.replace('y1="543"', 'y1="527"').replace('y2="543"', 'y2="527"')

block.text:
The horizontal skewer is better: it reads as skewers, no legs. However, the skewer line is thin and the meat cubes look like marshmallows? They read as meat on a stick. The second skewer behind is visible. Good.

But the helmet now looks like a **construction hard hat** even more with the flat brim? The wide brim is good; the dome is still smooth and green. The 兵 is large-ish. It's still ambiguous. Maybe because the helmet is front-on and the brim is symmetric, plus the color and sheen. A military helmet often has a **camouflage cover** with a rough texture and a **chinstrap** hanging. We have camo but subtle. Increase camo contrast, add a **band** with a buckle, and make the dome slightly **flatter and wider**. Add a subtle **dent/scratch**. Also, the **rim** should be narrower at the front? Hmm.

Maybe the issue is the **helmet is too clean and toy-like**. A rugged military helmet with a camo cover, scuffed edges, and a cloth band would read better. We can:
- Add a **camo pattern** with 4-5 larger blobs in olive_dk/olive_lt at 45% opacity, covering the dome. This will instantly say military.
- Add a **textured band** around the base with a stitched edge.
- Add a **small piece of cloth/strap** hanging from the brim on one side, not symmetrical.
- Make the dome **asymmetric** with a slight dent on one side.
- Add **scratches** (thin cream lines at 10% opacity) — maybe too detailed.
- Use a darker, more desaturated olive (#48522A) with less gradient; the current highlight is strong. Reduce gradient contrast, make it matte.
- The 兵 should look stenciled, not printed; add slight rough edges? Hard in SVG. Could use a stencil font (not available for Chinese) or a slight offset. No.
- Add a **star** above the 兵? no.

Maybe a **boonie hat** would be more obviously military and camping, but less iconic. A helmet is fine.

Wait, the helmet shape has a **very wide brim that curves down at the sides** and a high dome. This is actually a **pith helmet** / safari hat, not a hard hat. Combined with the 兵, it could read as a pith helmet (colonial). Not ideal. A modern military helmet should have a **shorter brim** and a **lower dome with side rails**. The brim should be close to the head, not a full wide disc. Our brim extends 50px beyond the dome on each side, making it look like a hat. Reduce the brim extension to 25px and make it follow the dome's lower edge. M1 helmet brim extends maybe 10-15% of width. Current dome width 284, brim width 330 (+46 total, 23 each). That's 8% each; okay. But the brim is at the very bottom and flat, creating a hat look. Real M1 brim curves down around the sides, and the dome sits inside. Hmm.

Maybe **remove the 360° brim** and use a **combat helmet** shape with a small front visor and side ear covers. A modern helmet (ACH/MICH) has a higher cut, no wide brim, with side rails and a NVG mount. That would read tactical/military, not hard hat, but more "special forces" than "兵哥". It might look too tactical for BBQ. 
- Add an **NVG mount** on the front (a small bracket) and side rails, which are unmistakably military. But then the 兵 badge would conflict. Could put a small 兵 on the side. 
- A modern helmet with ear protection and a headset could look cool but too SWAT.

Alternatively, use a **steel helmet with a camo net** — add a net pattern (diamond grid) over the dome. A camo net is unmistakably military and adds texture. The 兵 can sit on top of the net as a badge. This could look great and solve the hard-hat issue. But a net pattern at small size may moiré. Use large diamond lines at low opacity, maybe 8 lines. 
- A camo net with small leaves? Too much.

Maybe the brand doesn't need a helmet at all. Let's consider a **tent-shaped badge** with a fire and skewers, plus a **small helmet icon** on a patch. The main icon would be a **campfire under a tent**. Military green and camping, no hard hat ambiguity. The "兵哥" name is in the wordmark. A small **star** or **helmet silhouette** can be a secondary mark. This might be more appetizing and cohesive.

What if the central icon is a **campfire with a grill grate and a tent in the background**, and the badge's top has a **small helmet crest** replacing the star? Then the helmet is small and clearly a military accent, not the main subject. The fire/skewers dominate. That could be better for a BBQ brand.

Design:
- Circular cream patch.
- Background: pine trees + tent.
- Center: a large campfire with a **grill grate** across it, and 2 skewers with meat.
- Top: a small **helmet** silhouette (maybe 100px wide) sitting above the fire like a crest, or a **military star**.
- Text below.
- The helmet is small enough not to look like a hard hat, and the fire/skewers are the main icon.
But the user wants "兵哥" — the helmet is the only military cue besides color. A small helmet crest could work. 
- Or the tent itself has a **helmet** on top? Weird.

Alternatively, use a **soldier's dog tag** shape as the badge, with a flame and skewer. Military + BBQ without helmet. A dog tag is a strong military symbol, but it's associated with casualties; not ideal for food. A **military badge/shield** is safer.

Let's not abandon the helmet yet. It is distinctive and ties to "兵哥". We can make it look like a **military helmet with a camo cover** by adding a net and a more rugged shape. At 80px, it will read as a helmet because of the chin strap and wide brim. The current image at 1024 already reads as a helmet to me, but also hard hat. With a camo net, it will clearly be military.

Let's test a camo net:
- Clip to dome.
- Draw diagonal lines both directions every 18px, stroke olive_dk/olive_lt at opacity .25, width 1.5. A diamond net over the dome. At 1024, visible; at 80, becomes texture. 
- Add 2-3 small irregular **camo blobs** under the net at 30%.
- Add a **band** at the base with a small buckle.
- Add a **cloth strap** hanging from the brim on the left with a brass tip (asymmetry).
- Flatten the dome a bit more and reduce the gloss.

Let's try. Also, the 兵 could be smaller (48px) so it doesn't dominate; a stenciled unit marking. At 1024, 48*1.7=82px, still readable. Current 64*1.7=109px, large. Reduce to 52.

The fire: the flames look like a **leaf** or **tulip**, not fire. The central white core is a leaf shape. Need more flame tongues and a hotter, more dynamic shape. Add side tongues that curl outward, and make the outer flame edges wavy. Current path is symmetrical and smooth. A more realistic flame:
```
M 300 360
C 310 390 326 402 332 424
C 344 414 348 400 344 384
C 366 408 376 438 364 464
C 354 486 330 500 300 500
C 266 500 240 484 234 460
C 228 438 238 416 254 398
C 250 416 254 432 268 444
C 266 416 282 392 300 360 Z
```
This has two side curls. Add a second inner flame offset, and a core. The current flame has a big central white core that looks like a leaf; reduce the core size and make it a teardrop. Add 2-3 small embers. 
- At small size, a simple orange flame is fine. The current one reads as fire because of color, but the shape could be better.
- Add **smoke**? no.

The meat cubes: 3 cubes in a row, good. They look like **marshmallows** because they are light brown with rounded edges and a highlight. Make them darker, more charred, with grill marks (diagonal dark lines) and irregular edges (polygon instead of rounded rect). Use a charred crust #7A351C with a lighter center #B25E2E; grill marks. This will look appetizing. 
- Current cubes are square-ish with a dark border and a light top, reading as marshmallows. Add 2 diagonal grill lines on each, and a slight irregular shape.
- Draw meat as a rounded polygon with a charred edge.

The wordmark: strong, but the 4 characters are very wide and heavy, maybe too heavy (font 900). It looks like a supermarket brand. For a rugged BBQ, a heavier, slightly condensed font would be better. Noto Sans SC 900 is heavy and wide. Could use **Noto Sans SC 700** with a slight horizontal scale (0.92) to condense. Or use **Noto Serif SC 900** for a more crafted/rustic feel? A bold serif Chinese wordmark could look premium and BBQ/smokehouse, but maybe too traditional. The current sans is modern and clean, good for delivery. 
- Add a **grunge/stencil** cut to one stroke? Hard.
- Use a **custom ligature**: the four characters with a small flame replacing the dot? No.
- Maybe make "兵哥" in cream and "烧烤" in a warm **amber** to add appetite. But legibility and brand consistency. Could try "兵哥" cream, "烧烤" orange/amber. This would visually separate the name and category, and add color. At 1024, amber on dark green is readable. Let's test. It might look more food-brand. But two-tone wordmarks can look dated. 
- Alternatively, add a small **orange flame** above the "烤" or a **brush underline** in orange beneath "烧烤". A hand-painted orange underline adds warmth/rustic. But the wordmark is clean; a single orange bar under the last two chars could be nice. 
- For delivery, the wordmark must be legible. Keep one color.

The layout with the badge and text is good. The bottom tagline is still there, too close to the bottom border. Remove it or make it 18px at 0.6. Let's remove to clean up. Then the English can move down to 890, and maybe add a small orange rule at 920. Hmm.

Let's test:
- Remove tagline.
- English at 886.
- Add a short **orange line** 60px wide at y=920, centered? That might look like a design element. Or leave empty. The bottom margin 1024-900=124, similar to top 100. Balanced.
- Badge top 94, bottom 666; text 690-900. Top margin 94, bottom 124. Good. No tagline needed.

The patch tag "野营炭烤" inside badge: it currently overlaps the stitched ring and is hard to read. Remove it. Then the icon is cleaner. The square has the tagline removed, so the "野营炭烤" message would be lost except pines/tent. That's okay; the visual conveys camping. But maybe keep a small tag inside the badge at a better position:
- Move the badge tag to y=536, font 20, letter-spacing 5, with no lines. The stitched ring bottom 554, so text bottom 542, 12px clear. The fire bottom 512, 24px gap. It fits. At 1024, 34px. Could work. 
- The tag sits in the bottom of the badge like a patch label. It adds "野营炭烤". In the current image, the dash ring passes through the text because baseline 551. Moving up 15px fixes it. Let's do that and see. If it still feels cluttered, remove.

Current tag line at y=543 and text 551; lines/dots at 543. Move lines to 527, text baseline 535, font 21. Fire bottom 512, so lines at 527 are 15px below. Text bottom 541, ring at 554. Good. The tag might overlap the logs at 507? no. This could look good.

But the patch's bottom area is narrow; 4 chars at 21px + tracking 7 = 105 wide, fits. Fine.

Let's implement these refinements:
1. Camo net + matte helmet, smaller 兵.
2. Better flame shape and charred meat.
3. Move badge tag up.
4. Remove square bottom tagline.
5. Maybe adjust icon centering up 10.

Then inspect at 1024, 512, 160, 80.

Let's first fix the tag and bottom tagline, and make helmet/meat/flame changes. This is iterative; need not overdo.

Camo net implementation:
```
<g clip-path="url(#domeClip)" opacity=".55">
  for i in range(-10, 20):
    line from (x, 160) to (x+160, 320) etc
```
Need cover dome x 158-442, y 166-312. Draw diagonal lines at 45° and -45°, spacing 24, stroke olive_dk, opacity .22, width 2. Clip. This makes a net. At 1024, 2*1.7=3.4px, visible. At 80, 0.27px, invisible; fine. 
- Add small knots at intersections? Too much.
- Draw 4 camo blobs under net at 0.35.
- The net may look like a fishnet, but on a helmet it's a camo net. Add a few small leaf shapes? Maybe not.
- A net plus 兵 may be busy. The 兵 could sit on a small solid patch (cream rectangle/circle) on top of the net, like a stencil plate. Hmm.
- Maybe skip the net and use stronger camo blobs. A camo cover with 4 big blobs is enough. The issue is more the shape than texture.

Let's compare: current camo blobs are subtle, almost invisible. Increase to 0.45 and use 3 colors (dark olive, light olive, sand?). A camo pattern with **sand/tan** blobs would add contrast and military feel, but may clash with cream. Use olive_dk and olive_lt only. At 1024, visible; at 80, texture. 
- Add a **helmet band** in dark olive with a small brass buckle on the right side. This is a strong military cue (chinstrap band).
- Add a **small cloth tag** hanging from the left brim, olive with a brass tip. Asymmetry = realism.
- Add a **dent** on the dome: a subtle dark crescent near the top right. 
- Reduce the glossy highlight: current left highlight is 0.42; reduce to .25. The gradient also lightens top-left; make it more uniform.

Helmet shape: maybe make the dome **slightly wider at the base and narrower at the top**, more like an M1:
`M 158 312 C 156 230 198 164 300 164 C 402 164 444 230 442 312 Z` — current. The top is very rounded. M1 has a more **hemispherical** dome, okay.
- Add a **front brim lip** that dips in the center: current brim path has a center dip? It goes from 136,312 to 464,312 with control points 190,299 and 410,299, so the center is at y~299 (higher), while the edges at 312 (lower). That means the brim **rises** in the center, like a cowboy hat, not dips. That's why it looks like a hat! For a helmet, the brim should be roughly level or dip slightly in the front center. Flip: `M 136 312 C 190 320 410 320 464 312` so center is lower (y~320), edges higher. Then the brim curves down at the center, more helmet-like. The bottom edge similarly. Let's change:
  - `M 136 310 C 190 322 410 322 464 310 C 475 313 477 323 466 328 C 412 347 188 347 134 328 C 123 323 125 313 136 310 Z`
  - This gives a downward center curve. Combined with the dome, it reads as a helmet brim.
- Current brim looks like a **sombrero/cowboy hat** because it's upturned at the center. Fixing this is key.
- Add a **front rim** shadow under the brim.

Chin strap: current straps go from the brim sides down to 392, with brass buckles. Good. In the image, they look like a chin strap. Keep.

Head shape: the 兵 on the front might be too high; center at 240. Fine.

Let's change the brim curve and camo. Render.

Simpler: rounded rect but add **diagonal grill marks** (2 dark lines) and a darker, more saturated color. The marshmallow look comes from the light highlight and square shape. Add grill marks and darker edges.
- Use base #8F4322, edge #5E2713, highlight #B85E2F.

This is basically rounded; not much difference. Add grill marks; that should fix.

Core:

This is improved. Helmet brim now dips, looks more helmet-like. The camo pattern is visible but subtle. The flame is better. The skewer is clear, meat looks charred. The tag no longer overlaps the ring. The overall square is cleaner without the bottom tagline.

But:
- The helmet still looks like a **hard hat / safari hat**. The 兵 helps. The brim is now like a helmet. The dome is smooth. Maybe add a **helmet cover net** or a **chin strap** that is more visible. Chin strap is visible as thin lines ending in brass rectangles; at 1024 it's okay. At 80, the strap may vanish.
- The 兵 is floating on the dome with no patch; looks like a decal. Could add a subtle **stencil rectangle** or circular patch behind it. A cream 兵 directly on olive is fine.
- The patch's bottom tag "野营炭烤" is small and sits just above the ring; readable. It adds context. Good.
- The skewer's meat cubes look like **three brown blocks**; they need more meat texture/irregularity. At 80px, they read as meat. Fine.
- The fire looks like a **tulip** or **flame**; better. The skewers in front of the fire with meat look good. The background skewer is a thin line; okay.
- The pines and tent are very faint, almost invisible behind the fire. The tent is a dark triangle; at 1024, I can see it, but it reads as a dark shape. The pines are pale and okay. Camping is subtle. Maybe make the tent slightly more visible (opacity .35) and add a **door glow** in orange. That would strengthen camping. But it might compete with the fire.
- The badge has a lot of empty cream at top (helmet top 160, patch top 28: 132px), while the bottom has the tag at 535 and ring at 554 (only 19px). The icon is top-heavy? Actually, the helmet is large, and the bottom tag fills. The empty cream top is 132px, which is okay for a badge; it gives breathing room. But maybe shift the icon up? The bottom tag would crowd. 
- The badge circle is 572px, and the icon is 350px wide. The composition feels a bit small within the badge. Could enlarge the helmet/fire by 10% to fill, but then the tag. The helmet width 300, patch width 544; 55%. That's reasonable. At 80px, the icon is 30px wide inside a 45px circle; too small. For app icon, we should **zoom the badge** so the icon fills more: maybe use a simplified emblem with no pines/tag and enlarge the helmet/fire. The current icon at 1024 has a huge cream margin; at 80px, the mark is ~45px in an 80px tile, still okay but not bold. Could crop the badge to the inner cream circle (remove outer ring) or zoom in 15%.
- For the square logo, the badge is a supporting element; the wordmark is primary. Fine. For the icon, we can use a **tight crop**: badge diameter 100% with the outer ring cut off, or scale the icon within the badge. Maybe create an icon variant that uses a **shield** shape or a cropped circle to maximize the mark. 
- At 80px, the wordmark square's text will be unreadable, but the badge reads as a green/cream emblem. Delivery platforms usually show the logo at 80-120px; the name is also displayed separately, so the icon mark matters. The icon variant should be bold.

Could create two icon variants:
1. `logo-icon` — full badge on green, for app icon.

block.text:
At icon size, the badge fills well. The helmet still looks like a hard hat, but the chin straps and 兵 help. The skewer looks like a **barbell** or **dumbbell** because the meat cubes are rectangular and sit symmetrically on a straight stick. The background skewer is a plain stick; the front one has 3 cubes but appears to have 2? Actually 3 cubes but one at center hidden? It looks like two big cubes at either end of a bar, like a dumbbell. This is a problem. Need make the skewer look like food:
- Make the meat cubes **irregular**, smaller, and more numerous (4-5) so they read as a kebab, not a dumbbell.
- Offset the stick so the handle is visible on one side and the pointed tip on the other. Currently the cubes are at 0.33, 0.49, 0.65, centered, leaving long bare ends symmetrical. The dumbbell effect comes from two cubes at the visible positions? The middle cube might be hidden by the flame's bright core, blending. 
- Use 4 cubes at 0.28, 0.42, 0.56, 0.70, side 24. This creates a row of 4 smaller pieces, clearly a kebab. The stick extends more on one side. 
- Make the cubes **rounder/irregular** with charred edges, varied sizes. Add slight rotation offsets so they don't look like a machined row. 
- The stick currently is horizontal across the entire fire, which reads as a spit. A **skewer** with a handle and a pointed tip, with 4 pieces clustered near the center, would read better. 
- Make one end a **handle loop**? A bamboo skewer handle is just a stick; maybe add a small **blade**? No. 
- Angle the skewer more (e.g., -12°) so it's dynamic, and place 4 cubes clustered center-left, leaving a long handle on the right. 
- The background plain skewer at +8° creates an X, which currently looks like a second bar. It might be okay as a second skewer, but at small size it reads as a crossbar. Maybe remove the background skewer or make it shorter/behind the flame. 
- Remove the background skewer to simplify; one clear kebab is better. The fire + helmet + pines already have enough. 
- The front skewer with 4 cubes clustered center, stick extending to one side, will read as a kebab. Add a **pointed tip** at one end (already). 
- At 80px, 4 cubes may merge into a line of meat, which is fine.

The fire behind the skewer: the flame's bright core is partially covered by the middle cube, making the kebab look like it has a bright center. With 4 cubes, the flame will be more covered. Maybe move the skewer **lower**, across the logs, so the flame is mostly above it. Then the kebab sits at the base of the fire, with flames rising behind. The skewer at y ~470, flame from 360-506. The cubes at y 460 cover the lower fire, leaving the upper flame visible. Good. 
- Skewer from (130, 486) to (470, 455), angle -5°, 4 cubes at t=.3,.42,.54,.66. The cubes are at y ~477-468, near the logs. The flame's upper part is clear. This reads like skewers grilling over the coals. 
- The handle extends to the left at (130,486), the tip to the right (470,455). 
- Add a second skewer behind at (160,455) to (440,485) plain? It could read as a crossbar. Remove.
- At 80px, the horizontal meat line at the base + flame above = clear BBQ.

But the current composition with the skewer across the middle looks like the fire is cooking the kebab; that's good. The dumbbell issue is mainly the cube shape and count. Let's fix with 4 smaller, varied cubes and remove the background skewer.

Meat cube shapes:
- Use a **rounded irregular quadrilateral** with 4-5 vertices, not a rect. For each cube, vary width/height and rotation by ±4°. Add charred edges and grill marks.
- E.g.:
```
<path d="M -13 -14 Q -15 -16 -10 -16 L 11 -14 Q 16 -13 15 -8 L 14 11 Q 13 16 8 15 L -10 15 Q -15 14 -14 9 Z" fill=meat_dk/>
<path d="M -11 -11 Q -13 -13 -8 -13 L 9 -11 Q 13 -10 12 -6 L 11 9 Q 10 13 6 12 L -8 12 Q -12 11 -11 7 Z" fill=meat/>
```
This is still rectangular. Add a **bone/fat** highlight and irregular char spots. 
- Could draw meat as a **cluster of 4 rounded blobs**? A cube of meat is blocky. Real BBQ skewers often have chunks. Blocky is okay if smaller and varied.
- The dumbbell effect is because 3 cubes in a row with two visible at the ends and the middle blending. 4 cubes with varied colors will fix.
- Make the cubes narrower (24) and taller (28), and space them 22px apart so they touch, forming a continuous kebab. 
- Add a **charred crust** on the edges: a dark outline 3px. 
- Add a small **fat glisten** (amber dot) on each cube. 
- Add **grill marks** diagonal. 
- Vary cube colors: #9B4A25, #A5522A, #8E3F1F, #B25B2E.

Let's implement a `meat_cube` with a `seed` parameter for variation, and 4 cubes. Remove background skewer. Move skewer slightly lower.

Also, the **pines** are very pale and look like Christmas trees; maybe make them more like **fir trees** with a darker olive and more layers. They are okay as a subtle camp cue.
- The tent is invisible at icon size; if camping is a key element, make it more visible: a clear **A-frame tent** with a cream/orange door, placed behind the fire. At 80px, a dark triangle may be lost, but at 1024 it should read. Increase opacity to .4 and add a **cream outline** on the tent edges, plus an orange door glow. 
- Current tent apex 382, base 502, width 124; the fire covers most. The visible sides are thin. Move the tent **behind and slightly to the left/right**? If centered, the fire covers it. Move it to x=210 (left of fire), base 420-540, but then it overlaps the pines. Could put the tent on the left and pines on the right, asymmetrical. That would make camping clearer and add composition interest. 
  - Tent at x=200, apex (200,400), base (140..260,500), width 120. Fire at center 300. The tent is left of the fire, partly behind the left pines; pines on right. This asymmetry could be nice.
  - But the badge is symmetrical with helmet centered; an off-center tent may unbalance. Could put a tent on both sides? No.
  - Or keep the tent centered behind the fire but make the **door** a glowing orange triangle visible through the flames? That would blend with the fire.
- Camping is also conveyed by pines and the palette; the tent can be subtle. The user said "野营等要素" — pines + tent + fire + helmet is plenty. 
- For the brand sheet, we can explain the tent/pines. At small size, they're texture. Fine.

The **helmet chin straps** end in brass rectangles that look like **earrings** or **weights**. Add a small strap loop/buckle shape instead of a plain rectangle. The brass rectangles are 17x12, rotated; they read as buckles. Fine.

The **helmet band** is a dark strip with a thin brass line; good.

The **兵** at 56px on a 1024 badge is 95px, readable. At 80px, it's 7px, not readable, but it's a texture. The helmet silhouette and flame carry. Fine.

Could use the **spark** instead of 兵 for the icon, because at 80px the 兵 becomes a blob. A simple spark shape stays crisp. But the 兵 is brand identity. For the avatar, maybe use the spark variant (cleaner at small size), while the primary square uses 兵. That would create inconsistency. Hmm.
- Use 兵 in both; at 80px, it's a bright mark on the helmet, still recognizable as a character shape.
- Or use a **star** on the helmet in the avatar, and 兵 in the primary. No.

The user likely won't scrutinize 80px; they'll see the 1024 image. Focus on the main visual.

The **wordmark** at 152px is huge and bold; it dominates the badge. For delivery, good. The badge and text are balanced? The badge is 572 wide, text 620 wide. The text feels heavier. Could reduce to 146 so the badge is the hero. Or enlarge the badge to 600. Let's compare:
- Current: badge 572, text 620, gap 24. The text weight is heavy; the badge is detailed. At thumbnail, the text block is a big cream rectangle; the badge is a circle. 
- A logo should have the icon and wordmark balanced. Reduce text to 144, width ~588; badge 572. Better. English 23.
- Or enlarge badge to 600 (r=300), text 148. Top margin 80, bottom 680, text top 700. Tight but okay. Badge diameter 600 is 59% of width, text 600. Balanced.
- Current badge top 94, bottom 666; text top ~690. If r=296, badge bottom 676, text top 690, 14px gap; too tight. Move badge center up to 370, r=296: top 74, bottom 666. Top margin 74 (border 30), okay; text unchanged. Badge diameter 592. Slight increase. 
- The badge top at 94 is close to the top border 44; 50px gap. Fine. Enlarging may crowd. Keep current and reduce text slightly to 146. Let's see after other changes.

The **English** "BINGGE BBQ · FIELD GRILL" is good. The spacing is wide but elegant. Could change to "BINGGE BBQ · CAMPFIRE GRILL" to emphasize camping. "FIELD GRILL" is more military. Maybe "BINGGE BBQ · CAMPFIRE GRILL" (longer, 28 chars) might overflow. Current "FIELD GRILL" is concise and on-brand. Keep.
- Add "野营炭烤" English? The badge tag covers.

The **background** is dark olive with contours; nice. The top-right contours look like rings around a point off-canvas; okay.
- The border ticks are subtle; good.

Let's fix the kebab and add buckle details. Then render at 1024, 256, 128, 80 to check legibility.

Implement meat variation:
```
def meat_cube(x,y,angle,side=26,seed=0):
    h=side*1.12
    edge = ... 
    # base path with 8 points and slight random offsets
```
We can use fixed variations based on seed:
```
jitter = [(0,0),(2,-1),...]
```
Simpler: vary `side` and `angle` per cube, and use a rounded rect with **clipped corners**? A polygon:
```
w=side/2; h=...
<path d="M {-w+2} {-h} L {w-3} {-h+1} L {w} {-h+7} L {w-1} {h-3} L {w-6} {h} L {-w+4} {h-1} L {-w} {h-6} L {-w+1} {-h+4} Z" ...>
```
This gives an irregular chunk. Add a dark outline by drawing a slightly larger version first, then the fill. 
- For the meat fill, use a **radial gradient**? Could add depth. A linear gradient from top-left light to bottom-right dark would make it look juicy. Define `meatGrad` with stops #C9743C → #A5522A → #7A351C. Use `fill="url(#meatGrad)"`. At small size, fine. Add a dark edge path underneath.
- Add grill marks as dark diagonal lines clipped to the cube shape? Without clipping, lines may extend beyond the polygon. We can define a clipPath per cube, but many ids. Alternatively, draw short lines within the bounds, they won't extend much. Keep them inside.
- Add a small **char spot** circle at a corner, dark. 
- Add a **juice highlight** small amber dot/line at the top. 

Four cubes at t=.27,.42,.57,.72, side 26, angles with ±3 variation. The stick is 320 long; cubes span from x 230 to 370, a 140px cluster. That's a proper kebab. The bare handle on the left (130-230) and tip on the right (370-470). Good.
- If the skewer is at y 474→432, the cubes are around y 458→445. The fire's core is at y 438-487, so the cubes cover the core. The upper flame (360-430) is visible. Good.
- Maybe shift the skewer down 10: p0=(136,486), p1=(462,444). Cubes y 470-456. The fire's lower part is covered, upper flame clear. Better.
- The logs are at y 493-510; the skewer at 486 is just above the logs, looks like it's resting on the fire. Good.
- The handle at (136,486) is near the left pine base; okay.
- The tip at (462,444) is near the right pine; okay.

Remove the background skewer. But then the composition loses the second skewer; one kebab is enough. Maybe add a **second plain skewer** behind at a steeper angle, with no meat, to suggest multiple skewers. At 80px, it's a line; could clutter. Remove for clarity.

Add **sesame/char dots** on meat? No.

Let's implement. Also add helmet buckle:
- On the band right side, at (420, 298): a brass rounded rect 18x12, dark slot. 
- Add two **D-rings** at brim sides where straps attach: small brass circles/arcs at (160, 323), (440,323). Currently rivets cream; replace with brass rings? The rivets are fine.
- Add a **side strap** hanging from the left brim, with a brass tip, to break symmetry. Maybe too much with the chin strap. Skip.

Camo net: maybe add 3 thin diagonal **scratches** on the dome at 10% cream, suggesting wear. Could look like cracks. Skip.

The helmet still needs something. Let's add a **camo cover band** with a stitched edge and a **buckle**; plus a slight **dent** (dark crescent) at the top right. The dent:
`<path d="M 362 186 C 386 200 392 224 380 244 C 372 230 366 212 352 200 Z" fill="#2C3618" opacity=".35"/>` But camo already has dark blob. 
- Add a **fold/seam** on the cover: a curved line from top to brim, already has a ridge. 
- Add **two ventilation holes** on the side? M1 helmets don't have visible vents. Hard hats do. Skip.
- Add a **small chin strap loop** at the side. 

Maybe the hard-hat read is acceptable; it's a **military helmet** to those who know. The 兵 and chin strap make it clear. Don't overdo.

Let's implement kebab and buckle, remove background skewer, adjust text size 148 maybe. Then check.

This is better. The kebab now has 4 cubes and reads as a skewer. The helmet buckle adds military feel. The fire is clear. The tagline inside badge is readable. The composition is balanced.

But:
- The kebab is quite low, almost at the bottom of the fire, and the skewer's handle/tip extend into the pines. It reads as a skewer resting across the fire. Good.
- The meat cubes look like **small brown boxes** with dark stripes; at full size, okay. They could be more appetizing with a glisten and char, but acceptable.
- The helmet still reads as a **hard hat** somewhat. The new buckle helps. The camo pattern looks like shadows/reflections rather than camo. Maybe add a **camo net** or more distinct camo blobs. The dome's left has a large light blob and right a dark blob, looking like a shiny hard hat. Need a stronger military treatment.
- The 兵 is good but maybe too large; it dominates the helmet. It reads as a **hard hat with a 兵 sticker**. A stenciled 兵 on a military helmet is plausible. Fine.
- The badge tag "野营炭烤" is very close to the stitched ring; it sits inside but tight. It's readable. Could move it up 3px and reduce size to 20. 
- The pines are pale; the tent is barely visible. The camping element is subtle. If the user wants "野营", maybe strengthen the tent/pines. The pines read as trees; the tent is a dark triangle behind the fire, mostly hidden. I can make the tent **visible on the left side of the fire** with a cream outline and orange door. But it might clutter. 
- The badge's top is empty cream. The helmet top 160, patch top 28; 132px. The composition feels top-heavy with empty space above. Could shift the helmet up 15 and enlarge slightly, or add a small **arc text** "FIELD KITCHEN" at the top. Hmm. A badge often has empty space at top. But the icon could be 10% larger.
- The text "兵哥烧烤" is now 148px, still huge; fits. The gap between badge and text is ~30px. Good.
- The English baseline 880, bottom 890, leaving 134px to border; the composition feels bottom-heavy? No, okay.
- The border is nice.

The main question: does this look like a professional logo? It has a cohesive palette and badge system. The illustration is clean but a bit **clip-art / stock icon**. To elevate it, we need a more distinctive, ownable mark and less generic details. The "helmet + fire + kebab + pines" is a scene, but the execution is flat vector. A professional logo could be more stylized/abstract.

Maybe simplify the icon to a **strong silhouette**: a helmet with a flame-shaped cutout and a single skewer. The current scene has many elements. At small sizes, it's busy. For a delivery logo, a simpler mark is better.

Let's consider a more iconic mark:
- A **shield/patch** with a **helmet silhouette** whose negative space forms a **flame**. The 兵 character inside. Crossed skewers behind. No pines/tent. Military green + orange. This would be bolder and more premium.
- Camping element: a **tent silhouette** as the badge's background or a small tent icon in the wordmark. Could keep pines at the badge base.
- But the current scene is charming and conveys all elements. Over-simplifying might lose the "野营" feel.

Maybe the final can include both: a **primary badge** (detailed scene) and a **simplified icon** for small sizes. The primary is rich; the icon is bold. That is standard. We don't need one mark to do everything.

Let's create a simplified icon:
- Cream circle, dark ring, no stitch/tag/pines.
- Large helmet (top 100-330) with 兵, large flame (340-560), large kebab across.
- At 80px, helmet + flame + kebab clearly.
- This becomes the delivery platform avatar.
- The primary square uses the detailed badge. Consistency through the same core elements and colors.
- The brand sheet shows both.

This solves small-size legibility. The current icon variant (full badge) is detailed; replace it with the simplified icon. Good.

Now, improve the primary helmet:
- Add a **camo net** overlay. Let's test it on a separate variant to see. We can add a `net` option to helmet; render a comparison.
- Or make the camo blobs more organic and higher contrast: 4-5 blobs, some with hard edges. Current blobs are large soft shapes, look like shading. A camo pattern typically has 3-4 colors with irregular shapes. Add 2 small **sand** blobs? A tan/sand camo patch would be visible and military. But sand on olive might look like dirt. Use `#8C7A4A` (khaki) at 0.35. 
- Add a **net texture** with thin lines; it will be more clearly a helmet cover. Let's test quickly on a variant by modifying the helmet function to include a net, render just the icon, and compare. If bad, remove.

Net code:
```
<g clip-path="url(#domeClip)" opacity=".5">
  for i in range(-20, 40, 2):
    x = i*10
    <line x1=x y1=140 x2=x+200 y2=340 stroke="#2C3618" stroke-width="1.6" opacity=".22"/>
    <line x1=x y1=340 x2=x+200 y2=140 .../>
</g>
```
This creates a diamond grid. At 1024, line width 2.7px; visible. At 80, 0.2px; disappears. It may look like a net. Add small **knots** at intersections? Too much. 
- A camo net usually has irregular holes, not a perfect grid; a grid may look like a fence. Could use a **hex net** or random short lines. Hmm.
- Maybe not.

Alternative: add **3D form** with a **specular highlight** and **ambient occlusion** to make the helmet look like stamped steel, not plastic. Current gradient is smooth and glossy. A matte steel helmet with a rough texture would look military. Add a **subtle noise texture** clipped to the dome: random dots at 0.05. At 1024, it adds a gritty surface. At 80, invisible. This could help. 
- Add **scratches**: 5 thin light lines at random angles, opacity .15. At 1024, visible; at 80, texture. 
- Add a **dent** and **worn edges** (brass/cream chips) to make it rugged. 
- This would make the helmet less like a shiny hard hat. Let's add 3 scratches and a couple of chips on the brim edge. 
- But a logo should be clean; too much grunge can look dirty. Keep subtle.

Maybe the hard-hat read is because the dome is **too tall and smooth**, and the brim is **too flat and wide**. Reduce dome height and make the brim **narrower**:
- Dome top 180 (instead of 166), bottom 312: height 132, width 284 ratio .46. Flatter.
- Brim x 155-445 instead of 136-464: width 290, only 3px beyond dome on each side? Too narrow. A helmet brim should extend ~20px. Use x 148-452 (304 wide), extension 10px each. 
- The current brim x 136-464 (328 wide) extends 22px each; reduce to 16px each (x 142-458). 
- The wide brim makes it look like a hat. Reducing to 16px and flattening the dome may make it look more like a **combat helmet**.
- The 兵 and chin straps still convey military.
Let's adjust: dome top 176, width 284, brim 144-456, height ~130. This will look more like a **modern helmet** and less like a hard hat. But it may also look like a **bowl**. The chin straps help.

Actually, an M1 helmet dome is fairly tall. A **hard hat** has a high dome and a short front brim. Our full brim is the main differentiator. The current full brim is clear. Maybe the issue is not the shape but the **color/shine** and the **兵 sticker**. 

Let's ask: would a viewer recognize it as a military helmet? The chin strap, camo, olive, 兵, and full brim strongly suggest military. I think it's acceptable. The "hard hat" impression may be because it's a helmet, period. Fine.

The bigger issue is the overall **clip-art** quality. A professional logo would have a more unique composition. The fire+helmet+kebab is unique enough. The vector execution is clean. We can enhance with a **hand-drawn / stencil** texture and stronger typography. 

What if the badge is a **shield** instead of a circle? A shield would be more military and less like a patch. But circles are better for delivery avatars. Keep circle.

What if the wordmark is **arched** or **stacked**? Current straight is strong and legible. Good.

What if the badge is placed to the left of the wordmark in the square, not above? For a 1:1 delivery logo, a stacked lockup is standard. Good.

Let's check the icon at 80px to see what survives.

def card(x, y, w, h, fill="#232B16", radius=16, stroke_opacity=0.18):

        f'<rect x="{x}" y="{y}" width="{w}" height="{h}" rx="{radius}" fill="{fill}" '
        f'stroke="{CREAM}" stroke-width="1.4" opacity="1"/>'
        f'<rect x="{x}" y="{y}" width="{w}" height="{h}" rx="{radius}" fill="none" '
        f'stroke="{CREAM}" stroke-width="1" opacity="{stroke_opacity}"/>'

def lockup(cx, badge_cy, badge_d, word_y, word_size, eng_y, eng_size, style="char", show_tag=True, eng="BINGGE BBQ · FIELD GRILL"):

    tx = cx - 300 * s
    ty = badge_cy - 300 * s
    p = [f'<g transform="translate({f(tx)} {f(ty)}) scale({f(s)})">{emblem(style, show_tag=show_tag)}</g>']
    p.append(txt(cx, word_y, "兵哥烧烤", word_size, CREAM, 900, word_size * 0.04, "middle"))
    p.append(txt(cx, eng_y, eng, eng_size, C["brass"], 700, eng_size * 0.22, "middle"))
    return "".join(p)
